title: O002-D2 CASE Metric and Trajectory-Tracking Sensitivity
purpose: Test whether CASE persistence dominance is specific to MAE or whether physiology may better track future valence/arousal trajectories under RMSE or concordance correlation.

design.evaluation: Same simultaneous unseen-person × unseen-video cells as O002 primary/D1. For each test subject and video, training excludes all rows from that subject AND all rows from that video. Video identity omitted.

models.physiology: context + exact frozen 29 O002 peripheral features

learners.ridge: same alpha grid and training-only GroupKFold tuning as O002
learners.hgb: same frozen HGB specification as O002-D1

metrics.RMSE: Lower is better; emphasizes larger errors.
metrics.CCC: Lin concordance correlation coefficient; higher is better and evaluates concordant trajectory tracking.

design.uncertainty: Crossed subject×video bootstrap with 5000 replicates, recomputing pooled RMSE and CCC from out-of-fold prediction sufficient statistics.

decisions.PHYSIOLOGY_TRACKING_RESCUE: At least one horizon×axis has BOTH Ridge and HGB delta_ccc_phys_naive 95% CIs strictly above zero.
decisions.MODEL_SPECIFIC_TRACKING_SIGNAL: At least one physiology-vs-naive CCC CI is strictly above zero but no horizon×axis is positive for both learners.
decisions.METRIC_ROBUST_PERSISTENCE_DOMINANCE: All 16 horizon×axis×learner delta_rmse_naive_phys CIs are strictly below zero and no CCC physiology-vs-naive CI is strictly above zero.

firewalls: Post-primary sensitivity; cannot replace frozen primary MAE inference.
CCC improvement means better concordant tracking, not causal physiological necessity.
No universal physiology-null or phenomenal inference.
paper_role: Determine whether the CASE result is robust beyond MAE and whether physiology tracks temporal variation better than persistence despite worse point-error forecasts.
